content: These references include studies on the detection of HCV core antigens, comparisons with HCV RNA quantification, and their use in monitoring treatment responses, screening blood donors, and diagnosing HCV in specific populations such as hemodialysis patients or those co-infected with HIV. Many of the studies also explore the sensitivity, specificity, and performance of different assay methods, including enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA), chemiluminescent immunoassays, and nucleic acid-based tests. Additionally, some references discuss the correlation between HCV core antigen levels and other clinical markers, such as viral load or liver histopathology, and the potential role of these assays in improving diagnostic algorithms for HCV infection.
